lessons.correction: Strengthen ground army, increase defense, economy, and expansion. Continue production and technology.
lessons.mistake: Overextending with ground forces without proper support, neglecting upgrades or production.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate if the opponent transitions to air or if a major engagement occurs.
lessons.title: Ground vs Ground: Defend and Expand
lessons.when: Late midgame, both sides have heavy ground-oriented postures. Opponent shows Zergling, Roach, Queen. Own army includes Siege Tank, Marine, Reaper, Marauder.
lessons.why: With both sides committed to ground, maintaining a strong defensive position while expanding economy supports a larger army. Siege tanks and marines provide a solid core.

lessons.correction: Strengthen ground army, increase economy, increase expansion, continue production and technology.
lessons.mistake: Over-teching without sufficient army production, allowing opponent's Zerglings to punish greed.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when more information about opponent's posture becomes available, or when a significant event occurs (e.g., opponent attack, expansion).
lessons.title: Early Ground Threat: Flexible Response
lessons.when: Early game, opponent shows a ground posture with Zergling. Own economy is moderate with heavy expansion.
lessons.why: The opponent's ground posture suggests a potential ground-based army. Maintaining flexible development allows you to respond appropriately without overcommitting.

lessons.title: Midgame Ground Clash: Solid Core
lessons.when: Midgame, both sides have heavy ground-oriented postures. Opponent shows Zergling, Hydralisk, Roach, Queen. Own army includes Marine.
lessons.why: With both sides committed to ground, maintaining a strong army composition is important. Marines provide a solid core, but consider adding supporting units like Marauders or Siege Tanks.
